definitions.explanation: A round, hollow Japanese doll modeled after Bodhidharma, the founder of Zen Buddhism. Traditionally painted red with a bearded face, the doll is designed as a tumbler that always rights itself when knocked over. Used for goal-setting and as a good luck charm.

examples.english: The daruma is a symbol of perseverance (falling seven times and getting up eight).

notes:
ALTERNATE WRITING:
・{達磨|だるま} (kanji form)

ORIGIN:
・Named after {達磨|だるま} (Bodhidharma), who supposedly meditated for nine years until his arms and legs atrophied
・This explains the doll's armless, legless round shape

TRADITIONAL USE:
1. Buy a daruma with blank white eyes
2. Make a wish/goal and paint in the LEFT eye (⟦{左目|ひだりめ}→左目：29955_hidarime⟧)
3. When the goal is achieved, paint in the RIGHT eye (⟦{右目|みぎめ}→右目：29956_migime⟧)
4. At year's end, return to a temple for だるま⟦{供養|くよう}→供養：11444_kuyou⟧ (ritual burning)

PROVERB:
・⟦{七転|ななころ}び{八起|やお}き→七転び八起き：06141_nanakorobiyaoki⟧ (Fall seven times, rise eight) - the tumbler design embodies this spirit of resilience

FAMOUS PRODUCTION AREAS:
・⟦{高崎|たかさき}→高崎：noentry⟧だるま (Takasaki, Gunma) - most famous
・⟦{白河|しらかわ}→白河：noentry⟧だるま (Shirakawa, Fukushima)

COLORS:
・⟦{赤|あか}→赤：02842_aka⟧ (red) - traditional, good luck
・⟦{白|しろ}→白：13854_shiro⟧ (white) - academic success
・⟦{金|きん}→金：02666_kin⟧ (gold) - financial success
・Various modern colors available

MODERN USE:
・Politicians display them during election campaigns
・Athletes and students use them for goal motivation
・Popular as New Year decorations

COLLOCATIONS:
・だるま⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{目|め}→目：00525_me⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{入|い}れる→入れる：01098_ireru⟧ (to paint daruma's eye)
・だるま⟦{落|お}とし→落とす：01246_otosu⟧ (daruma drop game)
